chunk_findings.detail: The parity check treats every declared parameter that is not `cli_only` as a CLI argument, but the file’s own contract says differences may also be declared with `Param.mcp_only`. If a `gate run` parameter is declared `mcp_only=True` and exposed in the MCP tool, it is included in `public` by `not p.cli_only`, so `_mcp_props() == public` can pass even though the CLI has no such argument and `ddflow gate run ... --<name>` would still exit 2. The CLI-side public set must exclude `mcp_only` parameters (and the MCP comparison should include them separately) for this to be a real CLI/MCP parity test.

The only assertions are that MCP properties equal the non-`cli_only` declarations and that `force`, `reason`, and `rerun_failed` are declared `cli_only`; the stated invariant “the CLI arguments are exactly those that are not `mcp_only`” is therefore untested. For example, if the actual `gate run` parser accepts `--full` while `_gate_run_params()` does not declare `full` and the MCP tool has no `full`, `_mcp_props()` still equals the non-`cli_only` param set, the `full` parity test sees `full` absent from both checked sets, and the suite passes even though the CLI and MCP surfaces disagree on `full`.

chunk_findings.detail: `_gate_run_cli_dests()` decides “the CLI accepts this argument” from action `dest` alone: it returns every non-`help` action dest in the `run` parser after subtracting `GLOBAL_DESTS`, but it never inspects `action.option_strings` or actually parses `--full`. Because `gate run` already has positional actions (the `B-quota-meters` and `unit_tests` arguments), a `full` parameter rendered as a positional action, or an optional action with `dest="full"` but without the `--full` option string, makes `_gate_run_cli_dests()` contain `"full"`. If the MCP schema also contains `"full"`, `test_full_is_carried_by_both_surfaces_or_neither` passes, while `ddflow gate run B-quota-meters unit_tests --full` still exits 2 because argparse does not accept `--full` as an optional flag. The test therefore can go green while the reported CLI-side flag drift remains.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_run_parity.py:_gate_run_cli_dests

chunk_findings.detail: `_gate_run_cli_dests` does `parser._subparsers._group_actions[0]`, but `build_parser()` is a stdlib `argparse.ArgumentParser` (the same file later uses `argparse._SubParsersAction`). On that type `_subparsers` is the `_SubParsersAction` from `add_subparsers`, which has `.choices` and no `_group_actions`. Calling the helper raises `AttributeError` before either assert, so `ddflow gate run B-quota-meters unit_tests --full` can still exit 2 with `unrecognized arguments: --full` while the parity checks never run.

chunk_findings.detail: The test decides whether the CLI “carries” `full` by collecting argparse `dest` names, not the option strings the parser actually accepts. A CLI can therefore satisfy the test while still rejecting `--full`: if the `gate run` parser has an argument such as `add_argument("--full-suite", dest="full", action="store_true")` (or a positional with `dest="full"`) and the MCP tool has a `full` property, `_gate_run_cli_dests()` returns a set containing `full`, so `test_full_is_carried_by_both_surfaces_or_neither` passes even though `ddflow gate run B-quota-meters unit_tests --full` exits 2 with “unrecognized arguments: --full”. Since the acceptance is about the CLI accepting the `--full` flag, the test must inspect `option_strings` or parse an argv containing `--full`, not merely compare dest names.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_run_parity.py:_gate_run_cli_dests

chunk_findings.detail: The help-action filter checks `a.dest != "help"`, but argparse's `_HelpAction` sets `dest` to `argparse.SUPPRESS` (`"==SUPPRESS=="`), which is the default for `add_parser(..., add_help=True)`. Given that default on the `gate run` subparser, `_gate_run_cli_dests()` always contains `"==SUPPRESS=="`, so `test_gate_run_cli_and_mcp_expose_the_same_arguments` fails even when every real flag matches the MCP schema. The test does not isolate the `--full` drift.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_run_parity.py:_gate_run_cli_dests

chunk_findings.detail: The filter `a.dest != "help"` does not remove argparse's help action: `_HelpAction` is constructed with `dest=argparse.SUPPRESS`, so its dest is `"==SUPPRESS=="`, not `"help"`. If the `run` subparser is built with argparse's default `add_parser(..., add_help=True)` (the default for subparsers), `_gate_run_own_actions()` includes that help action. `test_gate_run_cli_arguments_are_the_parameters_not_declared_mcp_only` then builds `cli_dests` containing `"==SUPPRESS=="`, while the right-hand side is the set of declared parameter names, which cannot contain that sentinel; the assertion fails even when every real `gate run` flag matches the MCP schema. The earlier refutation only changed the `--full` test to inspect option strings; it did not fix the dest-based CLI/parameter comparison, so the help-action defect remains.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_run_parity.py:_gate_run_own_actions

The earlier probe only switched the `--full` check to `option_strings` and does not touch this path. `_gate_run_own_actions()` therefore still yields the help action, so `cli_dests` in `test_gate_run_cli_arguments_are_the_parameters_not_declared_mcp_only` contains `"==SUPPRESS=="` and the equality against declared param names fails even when every real flag matches the MCP schema. chunk_findings.detail: The new parity test asserts that the MCP property `full` and the CLI option `--full` are present together, but the diff changes only the test file and does not change either surface. In the state described by the intent (CLI `gate run` has no `--full`, MCP `ddflow_gate_run` documents `full`), `_gate_run_own_actions()` returns no action whose `option_strings` contain `--full`, so `cli_has_full` is false while `"full" in TOOLS["ddflow_gate_run"]["properties"]` is true; the assertion fails. Thus `pytest tests/test_gate_run_parity.py` (and CI) fails as written, because the reported parity gap is not fixed and the test is not marked xfail/skip.
